title: Phase Y Neighborhood Proposal
description: Bounded JSON proposal from LLM specifying which concrete neighborhood of moves to evaluate with exact DP. The LLM receives a concrete solver state trace and returns this proposal. The solver executes the proposal by mapping source/target lists + constraints to concrete candidate (source, job, target) triples, evaluates them with exact DP, and accepts only verified improvements.

move_family.description: Move family to evaluate. Y0/Y1: only insert_inter is supported.

source_machines.description: List of source machine IDs (M0..M{n-1}) from which to remove jobs. Max 5. These are the primary attack surface — the LLM selects which machines to try moving jobs OUT of.

target_machines.description: List of target machine IDs (M0..M{n-1}) to which to insert jobs. Max 5. These are receivers — the LLM selects which machines can absorb jobs.

job_size_classes.description: Job size classes to consider: small (p ∈ [1,4]), medium (p ∈ [5,8]), large (p ∈ [9,12]). 'any' is represented as ['small', 'medium', 'large']. Filters which jobs from the source machines are candidates.

max_candidates.description: Maximum number of (source, job, target) triples to evaluate with exact DP. Hard cap at 30 to bound DP cost. The solver generates all candidates matching the source/target/job constraints, ranks them by ranking_hint, applies diversity_rule, and evaluates up to this many with exact DP.

ranking_hint.description: How to rank the generated (source, job, target) candidates before selecting the top max_candidates. Determines which candidates get evaluated first.

detail.cheap_lb: Rank by cheap_lb_delta (estimated lower-bound improvement). Higher delta = earlier evaluation.
detail.s2: Rank by s2 score (handcrafted: 0.60*s1 + 0.40*lb_gain + 0.30*src_gap_density). Higher = earlier.
detail.random: Shuffle candidates uniformly. Each call gets a different order.
detail.cost_gap: Rank by source machine exact-minus-LB gap (EC - RLB). Higher gap = earlier evaluation. Rationale: machines where cheap LB is most wrong have most hidden re-packing room.
detail.slack: Rank by target machine slack (epsilon - load). Higher slack = earlier. Rationale: targets with room to absorb jobs are safer bets.
detail.hybrid: Weighted combination of multiple hints (weights TBD in Y1 implementation).

diversity_rule.description: Diversity constraint applied during candidate selection to ensure exploration across machines.

detail.per_source: At most ceil(max_candidates / |source_machines|) candidates from each source. Forces exploration across all requested sources.
detail.per_target: At most ceil(max_candidates / |target_machines|) candidates per target. Forces exploration across all requested targets.
detail.source_target_pair: At most 1 candidate per (source, target) pair. Maximum diversity — explores each permitted pair exactly once before repeating.
detail.none: No diversity constraint — purely by ranking_hint order. Best candidates win regardless of source/target concentration.

fallback_if_empty.description: What to do if the proposal generates zero valid candidates (e.g., no jobs matching the size class on the requested sources). Ensures DP budget is not wasted.

detail.random_same_budget: Fall back to random neighborhood with same max_candidates budget. Selects random (source, target) pairs from the full machine universe (not just the LLM's request), evaluates with exact DP. Uses same move family (insert_inter).
detail.top_s2_same_budget: Fall back to s2-ranked candidates from the full outside pool with same max_candidates budget. Uses the existing DiverseTrimmed outside pool.

rationale.description: LLM's explanation of why this neighborhood should find improvements. NOT used by the solver. Included for traceability — lets us verify whether the LLM's reasoning was sound after seeing execution results.

safety_constraints.no_arbitrary_code: The proposal contains only machine IDs, size classes, and enum values. No code execution.
safety_constraints.no_acceptance_bypass: All evaluated moves still go through exact single-machine DP. Only verified improvements are accepted.
safety_constraints.no_unbounded_cost: Hard cap at max_candidates=30 exact-DP evaluations per proposal. Upper bound on worst-case DP cost.
safety_constraints.invalid_proposal_handling: If source_machines or target_machines contains IDs not in [M0..M{n-1}], the invalid IDs are silently dropped. If all IDs are invalid → fallback_if_empty is triggered.
safety_constraints.empty_proposal_handling: If no candidates match source/target/job constraints → fallback_if_empty is triggered.
safety_constraints.duplicate_ID_handling: Duplicate machine IDs in source_machines or target_machines are deduplicated before candidate generation.

execution_mapping.description: How this proposal maps to concrete (source, job, target) triples that the solver evaluates.

steps.detail: Start with all machines in source_machines. For each source, enumerate all jobs on that machine (by position index).
Keep only jobs whose processing time p matches job_size_classes: small ∈ [1,4], medium ∈ [5,8], large ∈ [9,12].
For each (source, job) pair, enumerate all feasible targets in target_machines. Feasible = the target has slack ≥ job processing time p (i.e., the job can physically fit).
Cartesian product of (filtered sources × filtered jobs × feasible targets). This is the candidate set.
Rank by ranking_hint. Compute the hint score for each candidate and sort descending ('higher is better') for cheap_lb, s2, cost_gap, slack. For 'random', shuffle.
Traverse ranked list. Accept candidates that satisfy diversity_rule quota. Skip candidates from sources/targets that have reached their quota.
Keep the first max_candidates candidates that pass diversity. If fewer than max_candidates, evaluate all that pass.
For each selected candidate, run exact single-machine DP on the source and target machines. If the resulting schedule has total exact cost < current TEC, accept the move. Otherwise, discard.
If steps 1-7 produce zero candidates, execute fallback_if_empty with the same max_candidates budget.

random_baseline_spec.description: The random baseline generates proposals of the same structure but with random machine IDs instead of LLM-selected ones.

generation.source_machines: Random sample of [1, 5] distinct machine IDs from the full machine universe, weighted by exact cost (higher cost machines more likely to be selected).
generation.target_machines: Random sample of [1, 5] distinct machine IDs from the full machine universe, weighted by slack (higher slack machines more likely to be selected).
generation.job_size_classes: Random subset of {small, medium, large}, each included with p=0.5 independently. If empty (p=0.125), retry.
generation.max_candidates: Same value as the LLM proposal it is being compared against.
generation.diversity_rule: Randomly chosen from {per_source, per_target, source_target_pair, none}, uniform.
generation.fallback_if_empty: Fixed to 'top_s2_same_budget' (silent fallback when unlucky random picks produce zero candidates).

random_baseline_spec.comparison_unit: Single proposal vs single proposal at the SAME solver state (same initial schedule, same no_hit_streak, same round).
random_baseline_spec.fairness_guarantee: Random baseline draws from the same universe of (source, job, target) triples as the LLM proposal. Same move_family. Same exact-DP verifier. Same max_candidates budget. Same fallback behavior. Only difference: which machines and jobs the LLM selects vs which machines and jobs random selects.

example_proposal.rationale: M0 and M1 have highest exact cost (1498, 1204) and large exact-minus-LB gaps (158, 84). M8 has highest cost density (6.2). Moving small-medium jobs to slack machines M24/M23/M22 should improve TEC via re-packing. Attack the most expensive machines first.
